timeout_triage.anomaly_flag: 88 raw timeout candidates in this fresh full run is ANOMALOUS versus evidence-004.json's own full run, which had only 2 raw timeout candidates (1 confirmed genuine, 1 resolved to killed on isolated rerun). Working hypothesis: resource contention among ~7 parallel mutmut worker processes running simultaneously during the full run inflated apparent per-mutant test-execution duration past mutmut's computed timeout threshold (timeout_constant=1.0, timeout_multiplier=15.0), producing false-positive timeouts rather than genuine mutant-induced infinite loops or hangs. Raw full-run timeout status is treated as NON-CREDITABLE to the Condition-1 numerator until isolated triage completes -- confirmed by the triage result below: only 5/88 (5.7%) reproduced as genuine timeouts under isolated, single-worker, twice-independently-regenerated conditions.
timeout_triage.protocol: For each of the 88 raw timeout candidates: (1) delete mutants/ workspace; (2) regenerate a fully fresh workspace; (3) run the mutant in isolated `python -m tooling run --max-children 1 <id>` mode, record result #1; (4) delete mutants/ again; (5) regenerate another fully fresh workspace; (6) independently rerun the same mutant, record result #2. Classification: timeout+timeout -> CONFIRMED_TIMEOUT; killed+killed -> NOT_REPRODUCED (resolved killed); survived+survived -> NOT_REPRODUCED (resolved survived); any disagreement -> UNSTABLE_TIMEOUT_TRIAGE (no majority vote, no guess).
timeout_triage.diagnostic_only_note: Before this strict protocol was adopted, an earlier pass reused the SAME (already-generated, not regenerated) mutants/ workspace for isolated single-mutant reruns and processed 84/88 candidates (82 NOT_REPRODUCED->killed, 2 AMBIGUOUS). That pass is retained below per-record as 'diagnostic_only_reused_workspace_result' for informational/corroborating value ONLY -- it does NOT count as one of the two qualifying final reproductions for any mutant's final_disposition.

raw_mutation_effectiveness_metric.note: Primary/formal score uses the conservative numerator (unstable-triage mutants excluded, consistent with 'only confirmed timeouts enter the numerator'). The best-case bound (if all 9 unstable mutants were hypothetically credited) is provided only to demonstrate that the Condition-1 PASS/FAIL determination is ROBUST to how the 9 unstable mutants eventually resolve -- both bounds are well below threshold.

condition_1_evaluation.disposition: FAIL — criteria. Robust to the 9 UNSTABLE_TIMEOUT_TRIAGE mutants' eventual resolution: even in the best case (crediting all 9 as killed), the numerator (2223) is still 65 short of the required 2288; in the conservative case (excluding all 9), the numerator (2214) is 74 short. This is a substantial improvement over evidence-004.json's pre-remediation 81.97%, confirming Waves 1-4 materially improved the score, but Condition 1 does not yet satisfy the threshold.
